findings.message: This host did not provide a verified exact author model for the planning review.

Focused reviewability: pass. The plan opens with a one-line pipeline (contract → clean snapshot → detached clone → fixed runner → exact reconciliation → authenticated external store). It keeps all four load-bearing decisions and their rejected alternatives in the main review path. It covers all 12 scenario blocks with a real boundary and a confidence limit for each. Data applicability covers all 11 subjects, and owners agree with source-of-truth authority. Measurement has a reasoned skip, and the durable architecture record resolves. I spot-checked the subordinate 37-case map against the supplied test sources, and every full name I checked (route-order matrix, checkpoint, conformance, contract-identity, installed-copy currency) exists with the expected outcome. There is one blocking defect. The plan's new admission rule says any change to the bytes of an assertion source refuses before execution until a reviewed shipped contract is released. That contradicts the recovery action the accepted R4 scenario requires for 'a committed edit to required assertion source', which is to request an observation of the new committed candidate. Following that action is guaranteed to fail, so R3's 'one concrete recovery action' would be a dead end. The plan neither reconciles the two nor records the conflict as a deviation. I have several non-blocking warnings about how much the proof can establish and the no-network claim.

Assertion-source recovery action contradicts accepted scenario R4. Rule: the R4 outline row 'a committed edit to required assertion source' requires verification to report stale evidence and 'names the changed assertion source and requests an observation of the new committed candidate'. R3 and done_when require one concrete recovery action. Defect: 'Fixed assertion contract' makes the assertion-source digests in the shipped contract admission requirements. A changed body 'refuses before execution, naming the source and requesting a reviewed contract update', with 'no silent digest refresh', and the new contract ships only with a new runtime release. So in this condition, a maintainer who follows the scenario's action gets a guaranteed admission refusal. The plan never says which action verification emits here. If it emits the scenario's action, the action is a dead end. If it emits 'reviewed contract update', it violates the accepted scenario's expected output, and the scenario test would fail or be rewritten. Known deviations says 'skip: no accepted architecture deviation' and does not record the conflict. Owner: the design choice belongs to this Implementation Plan. The scenario wording belongs to the user through scenario definition. Viable choices: (a) keep strict digest admission, and return to scenario definition so the user accepts a changed next_action for that row ('requests review of an updated shipped contract'), matching the accepted-scope row. (b) Relax admission so a committed test-source edit can be observed under the existing contract, with semantic-change risk carried to the later certification. This removes the 'bounded to reviewed test sources' guarantee. Next step to resume review: record the chosen option in impl-plan.md. If (a), also obtain the user's scenario change and a fresh scenario review.

Tool binding may not cover tools that tests reach by absolute system path. The plan binds tools through 'a controlled tool directory with only the reviewed tool names', and says any newly required tool 'returns to contract review instead of inheriting an ambient PATH'. Several mapped tests build their own PATH: planning-review-route-order uses `${reviewer}:/usr/bin:/bin`, and execution-plan-contract-identity also uses `/usr/bin:/bin`. installed-planning-copy-admission resolves `which bun` from the inherited PATH. Executables loaded from /usr/bin or /bin (for example git, which, tar) can bypass the controlled directory. If the inventory resolves names only through that directory, a loaded input stays unbound. State that the inventory, and the start/finish/verification rechecks, cover every executable actually loaded by absolute path, or say why system paths are trusted platform identity.

No-network proof is not specified. Observe 'declares ... no network', and the Codex exception is 'not an exemption from ... no-network proof'. But the fixed lane runs the real Codex CLI for marketplace add/plugin add/list, and the plan never says how no-network is established. That is, there is no network-denied execution control and no observation of outbound attempts. Stripping provider credentials does not stop update checks or telemetry. Name the proof type and its confidence limit, or narrow the claim to 'no registry install or model/provider request'.

The unmapped-case proof may test the integrity-refusal path instead. The shipped profile's 'version and content digest are authenticated'. The integration proof for 'Unmapped delivery case' uses 'an installed observer distribution with a deliberately invalid shipped profile'. A tampered profile would most likely trip authentication and return an integrity refusal. The scenario requires the result to name the unmapped case and ask for a reviewed complete mapping. Say that this control uses a correctly authenticated distribution built from a profile that omits one mapping, so the test discriminates the unmapped-case refusal from integrity failure.

Binding the whole product tree stales the observation on routine edits to the observer's own ticket artifacts. Only the Work Log, bookkeeping fields and one named audit summary are exempt, and phase_anchors is listed as bookkeeping even though spec R4 names only status, phase, timestamps and Work Log. So any edit to this ticket's impl-plan.md, execution-plan.md progress, or tracked review-ledger files will make a successful observation non-current. That is conservative and consistent with R4. But the plan should state explicitly that the expected consumer must observe after planning artifacts settle. It should also confirm that exempting phase_anchors cannot hide a change to an accepted boundary.

Focused reviewability: pass. The Approach table is long but stays at the level of boundary and confidence limit, and contains no test paths or commands. The design-alignment proof references are repo-relative, as the rubric allows. The deep mapping and investigation detail are explicitly subordinate links, not a second design document.

I spot-checked the subordinate 37-case map against the supplied sources. Both declaration orders for each fallback outcome, the stale/approved/refused installed-copy currency rows, the six checkpoint metadata cases, and the shared exact-route assertion (inclusion and exclusion in one expected array) all match existing test names and assertions. The listed eleven-file lane is consistent with proof-map.md.
